Image 1 is the floor plan of a room seen from above: its bottom edge is the front wall, its top edge the back wall, its left edge the left wall and its right edge the right wall. Image 2 is the front view of the same room (the establishing view), taken from the centre of the front wall facing the back wall. Generate one photorealistic cinematic still of this same room, empty of people, from a new camera position: the left-side view: the camera stands at the centre of the right wall, at eye level, facing the left wall, so the back wall is at the right edge of the frame and the front wall at its left edge. Turn the camera for real: this view must not show the back wall's furniture head-on unless it is the wall being faced. Keep every wall, door, window, piece of furniture, material, colour and light exactly as Image 1 and Image 2 show them, seen from this new side; the room layout and furniture placement exactly match Image 1. Location: INT. SU YAQING'S LIVING ROOM. A bright, spacious, stylish contemporary downtown penthouse living room in cream, gold and soft grey. Back wall: wide windows with sheer white curtains letting in soft daylight from behind. A plush cream bouclé sofa stands in the middle of the room with its back to these windows, facing the camera, with silk cushions. In front of it is a round travertine coffee table holding flowers and a tablet stand on a pale rug. Right wall: an open doorway into the kitchen, framed in brushed brass, with a glimpse of white marble counters. Left wall: the opening to the entrance hallway, the way in, beside a low gold-legged console with a mirror. Front wall, behind the camera: a TV wall. Light comes from the window daylight and a modern brass floor lamp beside the sofa.

Avoid: people, readable text, logos, watermark, any door or window the description does not name.
